{{short description|Generalization of monads in category theory}}
{{about|the concept in category theory|the groups of vibrational modes|Polyad (spectroscopy)}}

In mathematics, '''polyad''' is a concept of [[category theory]] introduced by [[Jean Bénabou]] in generalising [[monad (category theory)|monad]]s.<ref>{{Citation|last=Benabou|first=Jean|title=Reports of the Midwest Category Seminar |year=1967|chapter=Introduction to Bicategories|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=47 |pages=1–77 |doi=10.1007/BFb0074299 |isbn=978-3-540-03918-1 }}</ref> A '''polyad''' in a [[bicategory]] ''D'' is a bicategory morphism ''Φ'' from a locally punctual bicategory ''C'' to ''D'', {{nowrap|''Φ'' : ''C'' → ''D''}}. (A bicategory ''C'' is called locally punctual if all hom-categories ''C''(''X'',''Y'') consist of one object and one morphism only.) Monads are polyads {{nowrap|''Φ'' : ''C'' → ''D''}} where ''C'' has only one object.
